newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court convicts Basque ETA's "Tigress".
newsitem.headline: French court convicts Basque ETA's "Tigress".

text.p: A Paris criminal court on Thursday jailed for five years a Spanish Basque guerrilla known as the "Tigress" who, police say, is among the most ruthless members of the separatist group ETA.
The court found Idoia Lopez Riano, 32, guilty of criminal conspiracy, arms violations and use of forged identity papers.
It also barred her from French territory for 10 years after she is released from prison.
The 32-year-old "Tigress", an avowed member of ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) since she was 15, was detained in southern France two years ago.
She is wanted in Spain in connection with 23 murders, including those of 17 paramilitary civil guards, and several car-bomb attacks.
A French court has already ordered her extradition to Spain, but only after she serves her prison term in France.
Lopez Riano told the court that she regarded herself as a Basque political prisoner. She said she did not recognise the court as legitimate and refused to answer the judges' questions.

Smiling broadly to friends in the courtroom, she repeatedly made mocking signs towards her French former companion Olivier Lamotte who was carrying her pistol when the two were detained in Aix-en-Provence, southern France, in August 1994.

Lamotte, convicted by the court of criminal conspiracy, was sentenced to two years in prison, of which up to 19 months could be suspended. He had already served five months in prison while awaiting trial.
"I was very much in love with her, and I tried not to care about the rest," Lamotte, 30, told the court.
"Looking at Idoia Lopez, one can understand why," prosecutor Irene Stoller said. "But without people like him, terrorists would be weaker."
The court also sentenced suspected ETA guerrillas Jose Ramon Naveiro Gomez and Juan Luis Aguirre Lete in their absence to three years each in prison.
In a related case, the court sentenced Daniel Derguy, a Frenchman accused of participating in several ETA guerrilla attacks in Catalonia in 1993, to four years in prison for criminal conspiracy.
Javier Magazaga Urrutia, another suspected ETA member detained along with Derguy, was sentenced to 10 years.
